source_text: Venio nunc ad ordinarias sententias eius, per quas proprietatem doctrinae suae inducit, ad edictum, ut ita dixerim, Christi: beati mendici, — sic enim exigit interpretatio uocabuli, quod in Graeco est — quoniam illorum est dei regnum. iam hoc ipsum, quod a benedictionibus coepit, creatoris est, qui uniuersa, prout edidit, nulla alia uoce quam benedictionis dedicauit:
pass_a_gloss: I come now to the ordinary opinions of him, through which he introduces the property of his own doctrine, to the decree, so to speak, of Christ: blessed are the beggars, - for thus the interpretation of the word demands, which is in Greek - because the kingdom of God is of them. Already this very thing, which he began from blessings, is of the Creator, who dedicated all things, just as he produced them, with no other voice than that of blessing:

choices.english: with no other voice than that of blessing
choices.why: emphasis on the Creator's method of dedication
rejected: with no other word than blessing

bible_refs.note: beati pauperes, quoniam uobis est regnum dei

pass_b_english: I now turn to his standard opinions, the very ones through which he smuggles in the distinctive character of his teaching — the edict, so to speak, of Christ: 'Blessed are the beggars' — for that is what the Greek word demands — 'because the kingdom of God belongs to them' (Luke 6:20). Even this opening move, beginning with blessings, bears the Creator's signature: he dedicated everything he made with no voice other than blessing.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies the implied scripture (Luke 6:20) which is required for the 'quoniam illorum est dei regnum' clause. Pass A and B are consistent with the Latin source.
source: 'beati mendici', english: 'blessed are the beggars'; source: 'nulla alia uoce quam benedictionis', english: 'with no other voice than that of blessing'
